DWP Supplier Code of Conduct

1.20 This guidance provides additional information to the schedules of your contract(s). provider guidance does not look to replicate or replace the details within your contract, and you are responsible for ensuring you read, understand and are complying with your contract.

1.21 You must ensure that any organisations with which you have a sub-contractual relationship also have access to, and have read, the Confident Future’s provider guidance.

1.22 If you have any questions which are not covered by this guidance, raise with your Employment Account Division Performance Manager (EAD PM) in the first instance.

Document retention

1.23 Providers must maintain complete documents and records in relation to Confident Futures for the period of their contract. The contract Terms & Conditions will set out the relevant contract periods and the Records Retention End Date.

Welsh Language Act

1.24 Providers are reminded of the need to comply with the provisions of Schedule 16 (Welsh Language) in providing the Services in the Welsh language. This must apply to all your staff and supply chain.

1.25 Details will be in the relevant schedules as set out within your contract.

The Employment Provision Provider Code of Conduct (“Code”)

1.26 The Code outlines the standards and behaviours that the government expects of all its providers when they are working with government, and how providers can help the government deliver for taxpayers.

1.27 Providers that contract with the DWP will be expected to operate in accordance with the Code. The Code can be found at Schedule 14 of the Confident Futures Agreement.

Obtaining a Participant signature

1.28 When obtaining a Participant’s signature, Confident Futures is not prescriptive about how the signature is obtained. You have the option to use one (or more) robust digital alternatives to obtain and store a Participant’s signature as part of the evidence of activities undertaken.

1.29 Participant signatures will continue to be monitored as part of the Performance Compliance Officer (PCO) Compliance Checking Regime.

1.30 If you are unable to obtain Participant signatures on any required forms, you must clearly demonstrate that all reasonable efforts were made to secure them. Ensure that each attempt is dated and recorded, with supporting evidence kept for compliance and assurance activity.

1.31 You are reminded to comply with UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and DWP security requirements when engaging in any digital delivery.

Digital technology

1.32 Providers are encouraged to use existing digital technology and explore the potential of new and emerging technologies, as part of the package of support they provide for Participants. This is both in terms of providing more choice over how the Participant engages with the provider and if appropriate, improving the digital skills of the Participant. This use should recognise the different needs of Participants and adhere to DWP’s confidentiality data sharing policies, security policies, and security standards.

1.33 The provider must be able to communicate with and receive communications from DWP in line with the DWP email policy. To note, use of technologies may require security risk assessment and Authority approval before commencement.

Confident Futures - General information

1.34 Confident Futures is designed for Claimants on the Universal Credit (UC) Health Journey who have had a Work Capability Assessment (WCA) and are assessed as having Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity (LCWRA).

1.35 The provider of Confident Futures will provide a voluntary offer of personalised employment, health and skills support. The Programme will be informed by the social model of disability and will focus on building engagement and supporting Participants to increase their independence, confidence, motivation and self-belief, develop strategies to manage their health condition, improve their wellbeing, and engage in work-focused activity, helping them move towards employment or other DWP provision.

1.36 The provider shall design and deliver tailored interventions that reflect the diverse needs, characteristics, and circumstances of the Participant. Wraparound support will address multiple needs, such as finances, caring responsibilities, housing, addiction problems, debt and link the Participant to relevant specialist services: for example, housing, substance misuse, education and training providers.

1.37 Confident Futures provides a maximum of 365 calendar days of support to a Participant. Once a Participant has started on the provision, they should be offered a minimum of 182 calendar days of support. The duration of the support offer may be less than 182 calendar days in circumstances where the Participant exits the programme early.

1.38 The frequency of contact shall be Participant led, although there shall be meetings no less frequently than every 4 calendar weeks as a minimum. The provider shall offer meetings every 4 calendar weeks, face to face being the preference, or via an alternative method agreed with the Participant (for example, telephone or video call). Contact may take place more frequently as led by the Participant’s needs and preferences.

Overview of Confident Futures

1.39 Confident Futures is a voluntary programme providing personalised employment, health and skills support for disabled people and those with health conditions to make progress closer to and, where right for them, into work.

3.116 The PTWA will consider, whether Claimants have a communication need (English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL), deaf, visually impaired, hearing impaired or have a speech impediment). Before making a referral, the PTWA will consider all the options of support, including whether other support is better suited to address the Claimant’s needs.

3.117 For Claimants, where English is not their first language or they have communication needs, such as hearing impaired, visually impaired it is the PTWA’s responsibility to ensure access to Confident Futures during the Warm Handover appointment. Following the Warm Handover, for all Participants where English is not their first language or they have communication needs, you will be responsible for ensuring these Participants can access all the services offered through Confident Futures.

3.118 Once a Claimant is referred to Confident Futures, you are required to deliver support in response to these needs throughout the Participant’s time on provision and, where necessary, adapt your approach to ensure clear appropriate support is in place.

Chapter 3d: Travel and travel costs

Travel

3.119 When your Participant agrees to attend a face to face meeting with you, the location must be within 90 minutes of travel from the Participant’s home address to your premises or outreach location. Where a Participant’s health condition limits their ability to travel, you are expected to make appropriate arrangements to meet the Participant, for example at outreach locations.

Travel costs

3.120 You are required to actively promote the access to funding for travel, childcare and other expenses to your Participants throughout their time on Confident Futures and ensure that they are no worse off.

3.121 You must ensure that you comply with current HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) Guidance if you make payments or provide benefits, such as travel cards, to your Participants after they have started work, which relate to that employment. You should inform your Participant that Tax and National Insurance Contributions (NICs) are payable and how this will be done. Failure to account for Tax and NICs that are due on payments made to Participants in employment may be subject to penalties in accordance with current HMRC regulations.

3.122 You must make your Participant aware of any out-of-pocket expenses which they can claim from you for their Initial Meeting, if they attend this face to face, and that they are offered access to, and reimbursement of any appropriate expenses at all future interventions whilst they remain on Confident Futures. You should advise your Participants of the evidence you will need them to produce to claim refunds for new clothing when attending interview or travel costs, such as receipts.

3.123 You are responsible for funding the Participant’s travel costs to attend provision. If the Participant attends interventions arranged by you, for example to undertake work related activities, job interviews, interventions or activities, then you will be responsible for funding their travel costs. You will be required to actively promote the access to funding for travel expenses to Participants throughout their time on provision. There is no requirement to provide a Participant with travel expenses once they have moved into work, however, should you wish to offer to fund travel costs, this will be at your discretion, and will not be claimable from DWP and must be funded by you.

3.124 If your Participant commences work, then you are not responsible for travel costs connected with that employment. Should you wish to offer to fund travel costs, this will be at your discretion and needs to comply with any HMRC guidelines and are not claimable from DWP.

3.125 Whilst your Participants are expected to travel by the cheapest method available to them, there will be occasions where some Participants will be unable to travel by the cheapest method, for example due to a disability. In these instances, you will need to refund any additional costs incurred, which you will have agreed with your Participant, considering all viable options prior to their travel. There is no requirement for you to cover Appointees travel expenses.

Childcare costs

3.126 You will be required to actively promote the access to funding for childcare costs to the Participant throughout their time on provision.

3.127 You must provide funding for childcare, to support your Participant in an activity that you have or are approving, where it has been identified as a barrier for your Participant to achieve agreed goals and objectives. Childcare needs to be provided by the following to qualify for funding:

carers registered with Ofsted

a carer accredited under the Childcare Approval Scheme, run on school premises out of school hours or as an out of hours’ club by a Local Authority

schools or establishments exempted from registration under the Children Act 1989 or operated on Crown property

Local tailoring and stakeholder engagement

3.200 You are required to build strong and effective relationships with PTWAs, employers and wider stakeholders. This is essential to the successful delivery of Confident Futures. You must utilise and build on the partnership and engagement approaches established through Confident Futures ensuring Participants are effectively connected to local employment opportunities and appropriate community-based support.

3.201 You must ensure Confident Futures is well integrated with local and specialist services within each CPA. This includes working collaboratively with relevant agencies to make effective use of local funding streams, expertise and provision, enabling Participants particularly those with complex barriers to work to receive coordinated and holistic support. Providers must actively work to avoid duplication of provision and ensure support is aligned across services.

3.202 To support the above requirements, you will be required to:

maintain strong, ongoing engagement with all stakeholders within each Contract Package Area (CPA) to inform the design, implementation and delivery of the Services the Supplier provides

strengthen collaborative working by hosting or contributing to partnership forums and meetings that promote alignment, effective communication and coordinated delivery with all stakeholders

adopt a joined-up approach to employer engagement, working collaboratively with other providers to manage national and large employer accounts whose vacancies span multiple CPAs

develop and maintain relationships with local employers and stakeholders to source suitable vacancies, work opportunities and progression routes as Participants become job ready

upskill employers, where required, to support them in offering inclusive, sustainable employment opportunities aligned with the needs of Participants

utilise and enhance links with local services, health bodies and community organisations to ensure Participants can access appropriate support and Provision that meets their individual needs

place a strong focus on addressing and ensuring coordinated support for health-related barriers to employment by developing and maintaining effective working relationships with relevant local health partners

engage with relevant stakeholders at appropriate intervals to share good practice, exchange information effectively, resolve delivery issues and align support packages for Participants, including engagement with:

Jobcentre Plus Partnership Managers

Employment Account Division (EAD) Performance Managers (or equivalent) of the authority

local authorities

training suppliers

employer forums

sector specific bodies

other relevant stakeholders as required

engage with organisations represented on established local Get Britain Working Partnership Boards in England

engage with organisations represented through Regional Skills Partnerships, Public Services Boards, Regional Partnership Boards and Regional Engagement Teams in Wales

take the lead in establishing and facilitating regular partnership engagement meetings where partnership forums do not exist within a CPA

3.203 Due to the particular needs of the Participant group, a focus on support for health conditions will be a key element of this provision. As such, you must develop and maintain effective working relationships with relevant local health partners to ensure coordinated support for Participants’ health-related barriers.

3.204 You should engage with relevant stakeholders at appropriate intervals to share good practice, exchange information effectively, resolve delivery issues and align support packages for Participants, including engagement with:

Jobcentre Plus Partnership Managers

DWP EAD Performance Managers (or equivalent)

local authorities

training providers

employer forums

sector‑specific bodies

other relevant stakeholders as required

3.205 In England, engage with organisations represented on established local Get Britain Working Partnership Boards.

3.206 In Wales, engage with organisations represented through Regional Skills Partnerships, Public Services Boards, Regional Partnership Boards and Regional Engagement Teams.

3.207 A proactive and structured approach to stakeholder engagement should underpin delivery, supported by a clear local engagement plan that reflects labour market conditions, stakeholder priorities, and Participant needs. This should ensure early connection with key partners and sustained, meaningful engagement to support effective service integration.

3.208 Expectations around stakeholder and local engagement should be evidenced through the Participant Support Summary and Delivery Review outputs. These should clearly demonstrate how engagement activity:

supports effective local integration

reflects labour market demand

enables tailored Participant journeys and outcomes

Employer engagement

3.209 A dedicated and structured approach to employer engagement should form a core component of delivery, aligning with Disability Confident principles and the broader aims of Confident Futures. This should include proactive engagement with a diverse range of employers, including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and those with limited experience of recruiting or supporting individuals with health conditions or disabilities.

3.210 Engagement activity should focus on building employer awareness, understanding, and commitment to inclusive recruitment practices. This includes promoting the benefits of disability inclusion and encouraging employers to identify and offer suitable opportunities for Participants.
